question: An e-mail that appears to originate from one source but actually has been sent from another
solution:
The correct answer is __**Spoofing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Spoofing**

 
• Spoofing is a technique through which a cybercriminal disguises themselves as a known or trusted source.
 
• **Types of spoofing -**
 
 
• Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) Spoofing
 
• Man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack
 
• Caller ID Spoofing
 
• **Email Spoofing** - Email spoofing is a technique used in spam and phishing attacks to trick users into thinking a message came from a person or entity they either know or can trust.
 
 
 
• In spoofing attacks, the sender forges email headers so that client software displays the fraudulent sender address, which most users take at face value.
 
• Unless they inspect the header more closely, users see the forged sender in a message.
 
• **In Email spoofing an e-mail that appears to originate from one source but actually has been sent from another.**
 
• **Hence the correct answer is option 2.**
